name: irreducible-three-entry-cycle-whose-pointer-phi-names-the-arm
rationale:
The companion to `irreducible-two-entry-cycle-through-the-state-machine-construction`, aimed at the part of `src/native/relooper.rs` that two blocks and one branch do not reach.

Three differences, each deliberate. (1) `%entry` ends in a SWITCH, so the edge into the cycle is one of three and `store_phi_edges` has to place the initial phi values per switch case, not per branch arm. (2) The cycle is three blocks entered at ALL THREE, so the dispatch state has three live successors rather than a ping-pong. (3) `%exit`'s `%pf` is a POINTER phi with three incomings -- `%base+0`, `%base+1`, `%base+2`. A logical pointer cannot be spilled to a variable, so the relooper must rebuild it from the arm the run actually took, and the rebuild is the thing under test: the value's OFFSET in the thread's four-word window is a direct readout of which arm the construction picked. An off-by-one in that mapping does not corrupt a number, it puts the right number in the wrong word, which no scalar-only case can see.

The fourth word of every window is never written and stays at its 0x9c fill, so a rebuild that ran off the end of the arm list is caught too, and so is a spurious extra store.

Metal runs the sibling `.metal`, the same automaton with one entry. The hand equivalence was checked by simulating both spellings independently over all 32 inputs before authoring, and it is checked again here: Metal's own output is byte-for-byte the sequence derived from the irreducible form. `input[tid] = tid`, so n runs 0..31 -- every entry case of the switch, every exit arm, and trip counts 1 through 31.

name: broadcast-a-depth-texel-into-every-colour-channel
rationale: is_depth selects the depth arm of a back-buffer copy whose colour and depth textures share Metal texture index 0, so only the depth read is bound at all. Six distinct exactly-representable depth values are read by integer coordinate and broadcast to all four float channels, so a wrong channel, a wrong texel or a colour-arm read shows immediately.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-nine-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 9 and receives exact float4 zero from all eight linked _uber_clear bodies. An eleven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: gainmap-helpers-carry-three-texture-handles-through-locals
rationale: Three helper objects each hold one texture handle in a stack local: the entry stores inputRGBTex, inputGainMapTex and outputTex into allocas and the inlined body loads each handle back out before sampling or writing, so the whole case runs on the local-pointer-field recovery path. The static sampler is linear, but every uv is (gid + 0.5) / 2 against a 2x2 texture, so the fractional part is exactly zero and each tap returns its own texel. Every rgb triple sums to an exact power of two or exact zero in half, which makes dot * 0.33333334 an exact float product; the headroom is 2 so (headroom - 1) * gain is exact too. Both products being exact is what makes the two fmul/fadd pairs give the same answer whether or not they contract into fma, and the remaining steps are one correctly rounded add, one multiply, an exact halving and one fptrunc. The four texels are pinned by hand to 0.3125, 0.4375, 1.667 and 0.078125 as halves, all distinct.

name: linked-single-radix11-zero-write
rationale: One invocation selects one bounded radix-11 FFT work item. Unit extents and strides bound every destination-temp write to the authored output. The linked scalar prefix supplies exact one, the linked complex prefix supplies exact zero, and the linked postfix is inert.

name: clamp-four-cube-faces-and-leave-two-untouched
rationale: A one-texel width makes the linear texel id equal to the face index, so a base of two and a count of five send six threads at faces two through seven. Thread five fails the count guard and threads at face six fail the face-range guard, leaving faces zero and one at their poison bytes; both early exits are therefore observable rather than merely taken. The remaining four faces clamp into [0.25, 0.75] from below, from above, from inside, and from both ends at once, with alpha passed through. Every source and range value is exact in half, so the clamp is a selection and not a rounding.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-four-2x1-output
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 24 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-three linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The complete 2x1 primary block at origin (2,0) is captured byte-exactly from the poisoned 4x1 resource.

name: single-instance-world-space-transforms
rationale: An identity instance must report identity world-to-object and object-to-world transforms; weighted column projections compare every reported float3 column across Metal and Vulkan.

name: stride-a-half-from-bfloat-element-through-the-nd-array-slice-copy
rationale: slice1DArrayData reads both of its element types out of one uint function constant -- `resultType = fc & 31` and `input0Type = (fc >> 5) & 31` -- so supplying 396 fixes the source as bfloat and the destination as bfloat and leaves one path alive out of the thirteen-by-thirteen table. The copy narrows through an intermediate the info buffer names separately at byte 8; this case sets it to 10 (half), which is what makes the conversion observable rather than a memcpy. The info buffer sets count = 5 below the 8-thread grid, which is the branch that skips the strided loop entirely and leaves each lane below count moving exactly one element: it reads source element lane * 2 and writes destination element lane, so the three lanes past count must leave the tail of the destination at its 0xCC poison. Both base pointers are byte cursors -- `src + (srcOffset << shift)` with shift 2 puts the source at byte 4 and the destination at byte 8 -- so a translation that lost either offset or the stride lands on the 0xDD filler between the live source elements. Every value is exactly representable at each step and each names what the intermediate does: 1.0 -> 1.0 -> 1.0, -2.5 -> -2.5 -> -2.5, 0.5 -> 0.5 -> 0.5, 3.75 -> 3.75 -> 3.75, 9.313225746154785e-10 -> 0.0 -> 0.0.

name: authored-four-iteration-loop
rationale: The literal count at buffer binding 1 is four, so the only backedge executes exactly four times and the selected output is the sum 1+2+3+4.

name: linked-single-complex-unpadded-write
rationale: One invocation is admitted by a 1x1 grid. Unit divisors and widths with zero left and right padding select source coordinate zero, the reference-size constant exposes one device-buffer slot, the linked complex prefix returns an exact nonzero value, and the linked complex postfix writes both components to element zero.

name: clamp-a-bloom-knee-fraction-at-both-ends
rationale: downsample_2x_bloom samples one 2x2 source block per thread and runs vfx_tonemap_threshold over it, and the only place the case is aimed at is air.saturate.f32 -- the clamp applied to %26 / (uni.field9 + %26), the fraction of the knee-scaled luminance that survives. Every other quantity is chosen to hand that call an argument outside [0, 1] and to carry its answer to the destination unattenuated. uni.field9 is -1, so with %26 = Y*Y + Y and Y > 0 the fraction is Y*Y+Y over Y*Y+Y-1: above 1 for the six colours whose luminance clears 0.618 and below 0 for the two that do not. A saturate that did nothing would write 2.84, 2.57, 1.66, -2.13 and -1.06 times the answer instead of 1, 1, 1, 0 and 0, and a saturate that clamped only one side would miss half the grid. The six clamped-high texels then reduce to the input colour divided by its own luminance, so each carries its own chromaticity and no texel's answer satisfies another's; the two clamped-low texels are exactly zero, which nothing but a clamp at zero produces from a negative fraction. uni.field0 is 1 and uni.field8 is 0 so the knee is (Y+1)*Y with no threshold subtracted, and the autoexposure scale is 1, which keeps the luminance the case picked. The AIR sampler is normalized, bilinear, clamp-to-zero, and the read coordinate is (2*index+1)/size, exactly the midpoint of the block's two texels on both axes; every source block is filled with a single colour, so the tap is that colour under any weighting and the case does not rest on the filter. VRScaleBias is zero so nothing shifts that coordinate. All eight colours are multiples of 1/16, exact in half; the destination is rgba16_float, and every component of every expected texel is at least 0.7 of a half ULP from a rounding boundary, checked against all 6^4 orderings the four air.dot.v3f32 calls could take under fast math, so no reassociation moves a single bit. The eight writes are disjoint and cover the destination exactly.
